{"command": "create", "path": "/memories/session/plan.md", "file_text": "# Plan: Fix Firefox rendering of tilted terminal

## Problem

On Firefox at DPR 1 (1920x1080), the tilted `.gs-started__flipper` card shows:
1. No antialiasing on the rotated card edges (hard staircase).
2. Sub-pixel tearing/shimmer during the typewriter animation.

Neither occurs in Safari/Chrome.

## Root cause analysis

Firefox WebRender promotes an element to a **raster root** when it has
`will-change: transform` and/or `transform-style: preserve-3d`. A raster root is
rasterized into a texture **in local space at 1x**, then the 3D transform is applied to
that texture by the compositor. Consequences:

- The texture quad edge is not antialiased -> jaggies on the tilted border/border-radius.
- Text inside is rasterized at local scale then resampled -> subpixel shimmer/tearing.
- Chrome/Safari rasterize 3D-transformed content in screen space, so they look correct.

The current code has `will-change: transform` in **three** places
(`.gs-started__flipper`, `.gs-started__face`, `.gs-terminal`) plus
`transform-style: preserve-3d` and `backface-visibility: hidden`. These were added
deliberately (see inline comments at GetStartedTabs.vue ~L427 and ~L470) to stop tearing
caused by per-keystroke repaints. So the current "fix" is actually the cause of the
aliasing.

The **real** source of per-keystroke cost: `.gs-command-row` is `display: inline-block`
whose text content grows one character at a time (`typedLauncher` / `typedSuffix` refs in
useCommandCycle.ts). Every keystroke changes intrinsic width -> reflow of the row, the
`<pre>`, and the card -> whole-layer invalidation. Fix the reflow and the layer promotion
is no longer needed.

## Steps

### Phase 1 - Stop typewriter layout thrash (unblocks everything else)

1. In CommandCycleRow.vue, reserve the row's inline size so typing never reflows:
   add a visually-hidden sizer span containing the **longest** option's full text
   (`launcher + suffix`), positioned so it sets intrinsic width, and render the typed
   text absolutely/inline on top. Alternative: compute a `min-inline-size` in `ch` from
   the longest option and apply as an inline style.
2. Add `contain: layout style` to `.gs-command-row` so invalidation stops propagating to
   ancestors. Do NOT use `contain: paint` - it would clip the copy/selector popovers,
   which existing comments in GetStartedTabs.vue explicitly rely on escaping.
3. Verify the cursor span keeps its position when the row is width-locked (it currently
   sits after the suffix span).

### Phase 2 - Remove permanent raster-root promotion (depends on Phase 1)

4. Delete `will-change: transform` from `.gs-started__face` and `.gs-terminal` in
   GetStartedTabs.vue.
5. Make `.gs-started__flipper` promotion transient: remove the static
   `will-change: transform`; add a `.is-flipping` class applied in GetStartedTabs.vue
   when `activeSurface` changes and removed on `transitionend` (with a 560ms fallback
   timer matching the existing cubic-bezier transition). Only `.is-flipping` carries
   `will-change: transform`.
6. Make `transform-style: preserve-3d` transient too: at rest set the flipper to
   `transform-style: flat` and hide the inactive face with `visibility: hidden`
   (driven by the existing `.-agent` state class); apply `preserve-3d` +
   `backface-visibility: hidden` only under `.is-flipping`. This is the change that
   restores screen-space rasterization (and thus edge AA + crisp text) at rest.

### Phase 3 - Antialias the tilted edge (parallel with Phase 2)

7. Give the transformed quad a transparent 1px outer ring so any residual texture-edge
   aliasing lands on transparent pixels: move background/border/border-radius entirely
   off `.gs-started__face` (make it `background: transparent`, add `padding: 1px`) and
   let `.gs-terminal` remain the sole visual surface. Today both `.gs-started__face` and
   `.gs-terminal` paint a background and an 8px radius - redundant double-painting.
8. Replace the `filter: blur(10px)` on `.gs-started__stage::after` with a pre-blurred
   `radial-gradient` (or a large-spread `box-shadow`). A CSS filter forces an extra
   offscreen surface that Firefox re-renders across the 560ms rotate transition.

### Phase 4 - Geometry and polish (parallel with Phase 3)

9. `.gs-started__stage` uses `aspect-ratio: 4 / 3` on a fluid width, producing fractional
   block-size at most viewport widths -> half-pixel seams between chrome bar and body in
   Firefox. Evaluate rounding the stage height (CSS `round()` or a fixed height at the
   >=960px breakpoint where the tilt is active).
10. Keep the existing `@media (max-width: 959px)` flattening and the
    `prefers-reduced-motion` block; extend the reduced-motion block to also skip the
    `.is-flipping` promotion if it lands.
11. Add an entry to docs/engineering-log.md recording that `will-change` + `preserve-3d`
    make Firefox a raster root (no edge AA, resampled text), and that the correct fix is
    eliminating typewriter reflow instead of promoting layers. This replaces the now-wrong
    inline CSS comments.

## Relevant files

- `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue` - `.gs-started__stage`
  (perspective, `::after` blur shadow), `.gs-started__flipper` (preserve-3d, rotateY,
  will-change), `.gs-started__face` (backface-visibility, will-change, background,
  radius), `.gs-terminal` (will-change, border, radius, background); RTL `:dir(rtl)`
  variants; `@media (max-width: 959px)` flatten block; `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)`
  block. Also holds `activeSurface` ref for the `.is-flipping` toggle.
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CommandCycleRow.vue` - `.gs-command-row`
  (`display: inline-block`), typed launcher/suffix spans, `.gs-command-row__cursor`,
  `__copy-popover` / `__popover` (must not be clipped).
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/useCommandCycle.ts` - `typedLauncher`, `typedSuffix`,
  `visibleText`, `activeOption`; source for computing the longest-option width.
- `docs/.vitepress/theme/components/TerminalChrome.vue` - chrome bar, adjacent to the
  fractional-height seam.
- `docs/engineering-log.md` - new gotcha entry.

## Verification

1. Firefox on a DPR-1 display (or `devicePixelRatio` forced to 1 via
   `layout.css.devPixelsPerPx = 1.0` in about:config) at 1920x1080: load the docs home,
   screenshot the tilted card edge, confirm smooth AA on the rotated border and radius.
2. Firefox about:config `nglayout.debug.paint_flashing = true`: during typing, only the
   command row should flash, not the whole card. Confirms Phase 1 worked.
3. Firefox DevTools Performance profile while the typewriter runs: no per-keystroke full-
   layer rasterize entries; frame time stays under budget.
4. Trigger the terminal <-> agent flip: rotation must stay smooth and the mid-flip frames
   must not regress (this is what `.is-flipping` preserves).
5. Re-check Chrome and Safari for no regression - especially the flip, since
   `transform-style` is now state-dependent.
6. RTL check: load `/ar/` (already open in the browser session) and confirm the mirrored
   tilt and flip still work with the new state-dependent transform-style.
7. Narrow viewport (<960px): confirm the flattened 0/180 flip is unaffected.
8. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: confirm no transition and no stuck `.is-flipping`.
9. Repo gate: `vp check --fix`, then `pnpm run ready`.
10. `pnpm changeset` for the user-visible docs-site fix.

## Decisions

- Fix is universal CSS, not Firefox-gated. Browser-sniffed `@supports (-moz-appearance)`
  hacks are a fallback only if a universal fix regresses Chrome/Safari.
- `contain: paint` and `overflow: hidden` are off-limits on the card interior - existing
  comments document that popovers must escape.
- Scope is the docs-site hero component only. No changes to `@pantoken/components` or
  `@pantoken/web-components`.

## Further considerations

1. Transient vs. permanent `preserve-3d` (Step 6): making it state-dependent is the only
   way to get true screen-space AA at rest, but it changes flip behavior more invasively.
   Option A: transient (recommended). Option B: keep `preserve-3d` permanent and rely on
   Phase 1 + Phase 3 only - less risky, but the edge may stay aliased in Firefox.
2. Sizer approach for the width lock (Step 1): Option A: hidden longest-string span
   (exact, font-agnostic). Option B: `ch`-based `min-inline-size` (simpler, can drift with
   non-monospace fallback fonts). Recommend A.
3. Whether to keep the blur-filter shadow at all - Option A: pre-blurred gradient,
   Option B: drop the shadow on Firefox only, Option C: leave as-is if profiling shows it
   is not a contributor.
"}

content.text:
## Plan: Fix Firefox rendering of tilted terminal

The current `will-change: transform` + `transform-style: preserve-3d` combo is the *cause*, not the cure. Firefox's WebRender treats those as a **raster root**: it rasterizes the card into a texture in local space at 1x, then applies the 3D transform to that texture. Result — the quad edge gets no antialiasing, and text is resampled (the shimmer/tearing). Chrome and Safari rasterize in screen space, so they look fine. At DPR 1 on 1920x1080 there's no HiDPI to hide it.

Those `will-change` lines were added (see the comments at [GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue#L427-L429) and [GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue#L470-L472)) to stop tearing from per-keystroke repaints. The actual source of that cost is [CommandCycleRow.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CommandCycleRow.vue#L169-L177) — `.gs-command-row` is `display: inline-block` and its text grows a character at a time, so every keystroke reflows the row, the `<pre>`, and the card. Fix the reflow and the layer promotion becomes unnecessary.

**Steps**

*Phase 1 — Stop typewriter layout thrash (unblocks the rest)*
1. Lock `.gs-command-row` inline size with a hidden sizer span holding the longest option's `launcher + suffix`, so typing never changes intrinsic width.
2. Add `contain: layout style` to the row. Not `contain: paint` — existing comments require the copy/selector popovers to escape.
3. Verify the cursor span stays positioned correctly once width is locked.

*Phase 2 — Remove permanent raster-root promotion (depends on Phase 1)*
4. Delete `will-change: transform` from `.gs-started__face` and `.gs-terminal`.
5. Make flipper promotion transient: `will-change` only under a JS-toggled `.is-flipping` class (set on `activeSurface` change, cleared on `transitionend` with a 560ms fallback).
6. Make `transform-style: preserve-3d` + `backface-visibility` transient too — `flat` at rest with the inactive face `visibility: hidden`. This is what restores screen-space rasterization, edge AA, and crisp text at rest.

*Phase 3 — Antialias the edge (parallel with Phase 2)*
7. Move background/border/radius entirely onto `.gs-terminal`; make `.gs-started__face` transparent with `padding: 1px` so any residual texture-edge aliasing lands on transparent pixels. Today both paint a background and an 8px radius redundantly.
8. Replace `filter: blur(10px)` on `.gs-started__stage::after` with a pre-blurred radial gradient — the filter forces an extra offscreen surface re-rendered across the 560ms rotate.

*Phase 4 — Geometry and docs (parallel with Phase 3)*
9. `aspect-ratio: 4 / 3` on fluid width yields fractional heights → half-pixel seams at the chrome bar. Evaluate rounding the stage height above 960px.
10. Extend the reduced-motion block to skip `.is-flipping`; keep the <960px flatten as-is.
11. Log the raster-root gotcha in [docs/engineering-log.md](docs/engineering-log.md), replacing the now-wrong inline comments.

**Relevant files**
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue) — `.gs-started__stage`, `.gs-started__flipper`, `.gs-started__face`, `.gs-terminal`, RTL `:dir(rtl)` variants, both media blocks, plus the `activeSurface` ref for the flip toggle
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CommandCycleRow.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CommandCycleRow.vue) — `.gs-command-row` and the typed spans
- [docs/.vitepress/theme/components/useCommandCycle.ts](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/useCommandCycle.ts) — source for computing the longest option
- [docs/engineering-log.md](docs/engineering-log.md) — new entry

**Verification**
1. Firefox at DPR 1 (force via `layout.css.devPixelsPerPx = 1.0`): screenshot the tilted edge, confirm smooth AA.
2. `nglayout.debug.paint_flashing = true` — during typing only the command row should flash, not the card.
3. Firefox performance profile — no per-keystroke full-layer rasterize.
4. Flip terminal ↔ agent; mid-flip frames must not regress.
5. Chrome + Safari regression check, since `transform-style` is now state-dependent.
6. RTL check at `/ar/` (already open in your browser session).
7. <960px flatten, and `prefers-reduced-motion` (no stuck `.is-flipping`).
8. `vp check --fix`, `pnpm run ready`, then `pnpm changeset`.

**Decisions**
- Universal CSS fix, not Firefox-sniffed. `@supports (-moz-appearance)` gating only as fallback if a universal fix regresses other browsers.
- Scope is the docs hero only — no changes to `@pantoken/components` or `@pantoken/web-components`.

**Further considerations**
1. Step 6 is the invasive one. **A:** transient `preserve-3d` (recommended — the only route to true screen-space AA at rest). **B:** keep it permanent, ship Phases 1+3 only — lower risk, but the edge may stay aliased in Firefox.
2. Width lock: **A:** hidden longest-string sizer (exact, font-agnostic — recommended). **B:** `ch`-based `min-inline-size` (simpler, drifts with fallback fonts).
3. Blur shadow: **A:** pre-blurred gradient. **B:** drop on Firefox only. **C:** leave it if profiling clears it.
Now implementing. Starting with the typewriter layout lock.

Implemented the Firefox fix across three layers.

**Root cause removed.** `will-change: transform` and `transform-style: preserve-3d` were making Firefox's WebRender treat the card as a raster root — rasterizing it into a texture in local space, then transforming the texture. That's why the edges had no antialiasing and the text shimmered. They'd been added to fight per-keystroke repaints, so they had to go last.

**[CommandCycleRow.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/CommandCycleRow.vue)** — every command option is now laid out hidden in the same grid cell as the live text, pinning the row to the widest command so typing never resizes it. The sizers are zero-height (`block-size: 0; overflow: hidden`) so they contribute width only — pinning height too covered the agent shell's placeholder. `contain: layout style` scopes each keystroke's invalidation; not `paint`, which would clip the popovers.

**[GetStartedTabs.vue](docs/.vitepress/theme/components/GetStartedTabs.vue)** — `will-change` is gone from the face and terminal. A new `selectSurface()` sets an `.is-flipping` class that applies `preserve-3d` + `will-change` only while the 560ms rotation runs, cleared on a timer and skipped under reduced motion. At rest the flipper is a flat context with the down face hidden by `visibility`, which is what restores screen-space rasterization. The face now paints nothing and insets `.gs-terminal` by a transparent 1px ring, so any residual quad-edge aliasing lands on transparent pixels. The drop shadow is a pre-blurred radial gradient instead of an animated `filter: blur()`.

**Verified** in the integrated browser: terminal face, agent face at rest (the flattened `rotateY(180deg)` correctly cancels the flipper's back-facing 165°, so nothing mirrors), and RTL at `/ar/`. All 1810 tests pass, `vp check` and markdown lint are clean, plus a changeset and an engineering-log entry.

Two things I couldn't do here: Playwright can't click anything on that page (every element fails its stability check — pre-existing, unrelated), so **the flip animation itself and the Firefox-at-DPR-1 result need your eyes**. Force `layout.css.devPixelsPerPx = 1.0` and check the rotated edge; `nglayout.debug.paint_flashing = true` should now flash only the command row while typing, not the whole card.

I also skipped the plan's fractional-height step — with the raster-root promotion gone, Firefox antialiases fractional geometry normally, so the seam concern it addressed no longer applies.

content.input: {"summary": "Fixed the docs home page's tilted terminal rendering in Firefox by removing the permanent raster-root promotion (`will-change` + `preserve-3d`) that was costing edge antialiasing and resampling text, and eliminating the typewriter reflow that had motivated it. The command row now reserves the longest command's width via zero-height sizer spans in a shared grid cell, `preserve-3d`/`will-change` apply only during the flip transition via an `.is-flipping` class, the face paints nothing and insets the terminal by a transparent 1px ring, and the drop shadow is a pre-blurred gradient instead of an animated filter. Added an engineering-log entry, a test for the new `suffixText` controller field, and a changeset. All 1810 tests pass; check and markdown lint clean. Flip animation and Firefox-at-DPR-1 confirmation still need a human eyeball since Playwright can't click on that page."}
